items.title: One Great Chart: A Stark Shift in the Mortgage Market
items.summary: At the end of 2022, around 10% of unpaid principal balances were on mortgages with rates of 5% or higher, according to Intercontinental Exchange data. As of this July, 5%-plus mortgages represented more than 40% of unpaid balances.

items.title: Why Mortgage Bonds Are at Risk if Rates Rise—and if They Fall
items.summary: There were nearly 15 million active, primary mortgage loans in the U.S. with rates under 3% as of the end of 2021, according to Intercontinental Exchange data.  Many homeowners were shielded from surging interest rates in 2022 with locked-in rates.  A much bigger portion of the mortgage market is now eager to refinance if rates fall and will be put off from doing so by rising rates.
